5-WEEK WAVE

Build. Load. Peak. Recover.

The current heavy week ends with the 130 kg deadlift. Week 0 starts Monday, September 21 as the deload, then the cycle repeats through Weeks 1–4. Accessories stay familiar enough to measure progress, but can be exchanged when recovery, equipment, or weak points demand it.

01RPE 6Technique

Top single, then 3 × 5 at ~70%. Fast, repeatable reps with about four reps still available.

02RPE 7Build

Top single, then 3 × 5 at ~72.5%. Add load while preserving the same depth, pause, and bar path.

03RPE 8Strength

Top single, then 3 × 5 at ~75%. Heavier and specific, but never a grinder.

04RPE 9–10Peak

Test one controlled single, then 3 × 5 at ~70% if form is stable. Accessories stay light.

00RPE 5Deload

3 × 5 at 50–55%. Restore movement quality, absorb the block, and make space for the 5 km benchmark.

WEEK 4 · COMPOUND LIFT

A deliberate path to one rep.

Take longer rests as the weight rises. Use safeties or a spotter, and stop the ladder if technique changes.
  1. 10 repsEmpty bar / lightest full-height deadlift setup
  2. 5 reps~50% of current 1RM
  3. 3 reps~65%
  4. 1 rep~75%
  5. 1 rep85–90%
  6. 1 rep92–97% · confidence single
  7. 1 repPR attempt · only with stable form

STRENGTH DAYS

The exact work after the main lift.

Every compound lift begins with the same progressive warm-up: light × 10, 30% × 5, 40% × 3, then three ascending singles toward the day’s prescribed RPE. After the day’s top single, perform three back-off sets of five at roughly 70–80% of that single. The accessories stay stable enough to track.

  • Bulgarian split squat or dumbbell lunge · 2 × 10 / leg
  • Leg extension · quads · 3 × 10–12
  • Leg curl · hamstrings · 3 × 10–12
  • Hip abductor + adductor or weighted glute bridge · 3 × 10–12
  • Calf raise · 3 × 10–12

  • Seated pec fly machine · 3 × 10–12
  • Triceps pushdown · 3 × 10–12
  • Seated dumbbell overhead triceps extension · 3 × 10–12
  • Dumbbell pullover · 3 × 10–12
WEDNESDAY · SHOULDERS

  • Lateral raise · 3 × 10–12
  • Cable upright row · 3 × 10–12
  • Seated rear-delt fly machine · 3 × 10–12
  • Reverse cable curl, hammer curl, wrist curl · 3 × 10–12 each

  • Shrugs · 3 × 10–12 if recovery is good

RUNNING WAVE

Faster without stealing strength.

Run on Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday. Thursday evening is aerobic cycling: easy Zone 2 work that builds capacity without adding another impact session. Pace follows effort for now; the measured 5 km time determines the next block.

Benchmark timing: Week 0 is the deload. Use its Sunday for the 5 km benchmark only if legs feel recovered; otherwise keep it easy and test the following Sunday. All bike sessions are conversational Zone 2 rather than hard intervals.

All lifting numbers are kilograms. Current shoulder baseline: seated dumbbell press at 16 kg per hand × 10 easy reps. Because that does not convert cleanly to a standing barbell press, the first peak establishes the comparable barbell baseline and recalibrates Blocks B and C. The final 5 km test is deliberately placed in the post-peak Week 0 so it is not stacked onto the same fatigue week as the December maxes.

PRINCIPLES

Train hard. Record honestly. Recover deliberately.

ProgressiveLoad, volume, and aerobic work evolve from recorded performance—not guesswork.
HybridStrength and endurance are treated as interacting parts of the same system.
RecoverableSleep, readiness, mobility, and pain signals constrain the next training decision.
Public framework, private records.Workout logs, body metrics, sleep, nutrition, and personal notes are not shown on this page.
